text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government has given the go ahead for planning for a superhighway running the length of the country along parts of the former Ho Chi Minh Trail.
-- The finance ministry and state bank are preparing to recommend changes to a decree issued last October governing financial management and accounting at state owned firms.
-- France will support a feasibility study into the construction of two elevated railway lines for Ho Chi Minh City.
-- State Bank governor Cao Si Kiem says the country's first stock market is unlikely to be established this year.

-- The People's Court in Ho Chi Minh city has sentenced two people to death and punished five others with prison terms of up to life on charges involving fraud and the appropriation of socialist and citizen's property.
-- The Customs Office uncovered some 12,500 cases of smuggling and commercial fraud during 1996, a rise of 45 percent from the level in 1995.
-- Hanoi city has set itself a target of 14-15 percent growth in Gross Domestic Product during 1997.
-- Hanoi's Party Committee has called for stronger efforts to prevent degeneration, corruption and to combat internal disorder caused by hostile forces.
-- The Government has announced the draft of an ordinance on the establishment of a sea police force.
-- The Ministry of Trade has issued new regulations on trademarks to tighten controls over the quality of consummer goods.
-- Philippine Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon arrived in Ho Chi Minh city on Tuesday to attend the opening ceremony of the Philippine consulate.
